Title: OEE

Write a process, that collects relevant information from a machine, and calculated the Overall Equipment Efficiency (OEE).

args.text: When a process description says that work or measurement continues after a system or machine is restarted, model a restart-waiting event that flows to the continuation of the work.

trace.reason: Check whether a documented guideline already covers resuming work after a restart.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.

args.text: When a process description says that work resumes after a machine or system is restarted, model the restart as a catch event and connect it by sequence flow to the activity that resumes the work.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers modeling a restart and its continuation.

result.rule: When the description says ongoing work should resume when an external trigger occurs: Model the wait for that trigger with an intermediate catch event, and connect it to the activity that resumes the work.
When the description states a process trigger followed by a subsequent activity: Connect the start event to the first activity with an outgoing sequence flow, preserving the stated execution order.

When the description indicates that an activity recurs at intervals during a longer-running process phase.: Model the recurring activity as work within that phase and connect it to the surrounding process flow.

When the description says the process begins when a participant performs an action: Model the process trigger with a start event, then model the described action as an activity after that event; do not use the start event alone to represent the action.

result.rule: Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.
Use bpmn:task for atomic work when the execution mode is unspecified. A task contains no internal flow.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.

args.text: When the description says that flow continues only after an external event or condition occurs, model the wait as an intermediate catch event rather than a task.

result.rule: When the description states that an activity initiates processing and that processing continues while other work takes place: Model the initiating activity as a task and the completion of processing as an intermediate catch event; do not model the wait itself as a task.

When the description says that work proceeds after items arrive, without stating a separate action to receive them: Model the arrival as an intermediate catch event when it is a prerequisite for subsequent work; do not add a separate receiving activity unless the description explicitly describes one.

When the description says that an external item or resource arrives before subsequent work, without describing a separate receiving action: Model the arrival as an intermediate catch event that the process waits for, rather than inventing a receiving task; use a message catch event only when the description establishes that the arrival is communicated as a message.

When the description says that an ongoing activity continues until a stated condition occurs, and then states an outcome that follows: Model waiting for that condition with an intermediate catch event, then continue the flow to the stated outcome.
